<!-- Hey there. Thank you so much for improving NewPipe, and filling out the details. Having roughly the same layout helps everyone considerably :)-->


#### What is it?
- [ ] Bugfix (user facing)
- [x] Feature (user facing)
- [ ] Codebase improvement (dev facing)
- [ ] Meta improvement to the project (dev facing)


#### Description of the changes in your PR
<!-- While bullet points are the norm in this section, feel free to write free-form text instead of a list -->
- Database migration
Add a new column `display_index (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)` in `playlists` and `remote_playlists`.
- A playlists merge algorithm
Implement an algorithm to merge local playlists and remote playlists by index. If they have the same index, sort them by name.
- Changing index
If the index saved in the database doesn't match the actual display index for some reason (e.g., setting to all zero after database migration, or a new playlist is created with index -1 (thus being on the top), or the index is not continuous after deletion, or the user changes the index), save the new index to the database.
- Debounced saver
    Save the list 10 seconds after the last change occurred. The logic is almost the same as the one in `LocalPlaylistFragment`.
    **Update:** now the code is reused.
- UI and Item holder
  - Create `list_playlist_bookmark_item.xml`. It's just `list_playlist_mini_item.xml` adding an handle on the right.
  - Create `LocalBookmarkPlaylistItemHolder` and `RemoteBookmarkPlaylistItemHolder`.

reply.body:
The debounce saver is first introduced in `LocalPlaylistFragment`. Everytime the change occurred, all the videos in the playlist will be deleted and insert again. (This implementation is a bit of silly, I think.) Perhaps deleting 100 records and adding 100 records when the item moves a single row. This will lead to heavy db load.

As for `BookmarkFragment`, the db load is not as heavy as that in `LocalPlaylistFragment`, since it only modifies records it needs to modify. I use the debounce saver in `BookmarkFragment` for consistency. But not using it might be fine.

timeline.body:
I don't understand why you need to store the original database index and all of the other data. I would do it like this:
- when initially receiving the items, just set them in the list
- keep a `List<Pair<Long, LocalItem.LocalItemType>> deletedItems` and when the user deletes an item, add its id+type here
- when doing any change (except deletion), do not update any variable except `debounceSaver.isModified`
- let the debounce saver or `onPause` call `saveImmediate`
- in `saveImmediate`:
  - delete all items found in `deletedItems` and clear `deletedItems`
  - cycle through `items` and if there is an item with a `displayIndex` different than its position in the list, add it to the items to update
  - update the `displayIndex` of items in the list
Instead of nesting things, you can just use some RxJava functions to do two actions in parallel and then calling `debounceSaver.setIsModified(false);` when both have finished.

```java
if (isModified != null) isModified.set(true);
debounceSaver.saveChanges();
```
everytime I want to save changes.

The original method is here. The debounce saver is integrated in `LocalPlaylistFragment` before this pr.

Are we sure we want to have a `DEFAULT 0` here? Maybe it is the right choice, but it's better not to have default values if possible. If you removed the `DEFAULT 0` you should add a `` `display_index` `` and a `, 0` on the line below obviously.

Why do we need an index on the playlist name? I mean, I get it that you just copied it from here: https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/8ad7bf60d7ed3bcde5bda0d601ae5d920c042eb3/app/src/main/java/org/schabi/newpipe/database/Migrations.java#L68, but since now playlists are not sorted according to name anymore, it is useless.

<sub>Maybe an index on `display_index` would be a good idea, but even then, maybe it's just overkill given that you need to rewrite the whole database when a playlist is added or removed. Oh, and probably it would be completely useless since you sort in-memory, so ignore this.</sub>
This, too, is now also useless.

```suggestion
    static void addItem(final List<PlaylistLocalItem> result,
                        final PlaylistLocalItem item,
                        final List<PlaylistLocalItem> itemsWithSameIndex) {
```
I don't think you really need the `if`

The fields in the `GROUP BY` are flawed. You should always group by **all** columns that you then want to use in `ORDER BY` or `SELECT`, otherwise, if a group turns out with more than just one item, it might be possible that the arguments of `ORDER BY` or of `SELECT` do not have a unique way to be chosen. But anyway, since this is the same as `getPlaylistMetadata`, it's probably ok leaving it like this.

timeline.message:
Fix inconsistencies when removing playlist

Remove checkDisplayIndexModified because it was causing more problems than it solved. Now when adding new playlists they won't necessarily appear at the top, but will get sorted alphabetically along with the other playlists with index -1. This will be the case until any playlist is sorted, at which point all indices are assigned and newly added playlists will appear at the top again.

timeline.body:
The 5 sonartype issues are due to:
- some code duplication due to both BookmarkFragment and LocalPlaylistFragment allowing to move items around (but it would make things just more complicated to try to deduplicate this, it's not so much after all)
- an empty onComplete() method (there's no action to do, and there isn't a specific reason for this, so no need to add a comment to the method)
- some "commented out code" which is actually a legitimate comment explaining what methods should be used for future reference
- constructor with 8 parameters required by the Room database

I tested, fixed some things and made the implementation simpler. I tested again and everything seems to work well. I deleted, moved, renamed remote and local playlists and there were no inconsistencies.
